bibl.title: The Thirteenth Catechetical Homily — ܡܐܡܪܐ ܕܬܠܬܐ
The second homily on baptism
bibl.author: Theodore of Mopsuestia — ܬܐܕܘܪܘܤ ܡܦܫܩܢܐ

noteGrp.note: On the rites of the renunciation of Satan and union with Christ and anointment of the forehead. The formula of renunciation: “I abjure Satan and all his angels, and all his service, and all his deception, and all his worldly glamour”. The union with Christ follows it: “…and I engage myself, and believe, and am baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit”. The renunciation means that the candidate will not have any relations with Satan anymore. The candidate should stop any relations with Satan “and his angels,” among whom there are pagans and heretics such as Mani, Marcion and Valentinus, Paul of Samosata, Arius and Eunomius, Apollinarius. “All his service” includes pagan worship and sacrifices, astrology, purifications, washings and different superstitions, observances of Judaism and services of heretics. “All his deception” means all pagan and heretical religious ceremonies, which fascinate and at the same time deceive the simple. “All his worldly glamour” means the entertainments of pagans, namely theatre, circus, racecourse, competitions of the athletes, profane songs, music and dances. After renunciation, a priest signs the forehead of a candidate. This anointment gives him or her parrhesia (freedom, confidence) before God.
